title: To those leaving for other countries
takeaway: Wherever you go, make your country proud and don't forget the people who love you.
scene: Many Pakistanis go abroad to work and study. This poem is the poet's advice to a loved one who is leaving: be good, be proud of where you're from, and don't forget home.

original: وچھڑ جاوناں سجن پیاریاں توں گل ایہہ کوئی صبر قرار دی نئیں
اپنے جوبن تے باغ بہار ہووے باجھوں سجناں رت بہار دی نئیں
transliteration: Vichhar jaavnaan sajan pyaariyaan ton, gall eh koi sabr qaraar di nahin
Apne joban te baagh bahaar hove, baajhon sajnaan rut bahaar di nahin
translation: Being parted from dear loved ones is not something you can calmly accept.
The garden may be in full bloom, but without loved ones it isn't spring.
couplets.story: Saying goodbye to people you love is never easy. Even if everything is going well, it doesn't feel like spring without the people you love around you.

original: ملک قوم دا اچا نام رکھیں وچ پردیس مصیبتاں آوندیاں نئیں
پچھے رہندیاں نوں بھل نہ جائیں احمدؔ تینوں یاد تے ساڈی وساردی نئیں
transliteration: Mulk qaum da uchcha naam rakheen, vich pardes museebataan aaundiyaan nahin
Pichhe rehndiyaan nu bhul na jaaeen, Ahmad tainu yaad te saadi visaardi nahin
translation: Keep your country's and your people's name high, so no trouble comes your way abroad.
Don't forget those who stay behind; Ahmad, we will never stop remembering you.
couplets.story: Make your country proud while you're away, and stay out of trouble. And don't forget the family you left behind, because they'll never stop thinking about you.

original: ولید لنگھیا فرنگیں ہتھ اوناں ملک قوم لئی راہ نجات دی لبھ
یاد پھلاں دے نال سجا دھرتی راہوں کنڈے ہٹا کے سب دے سب
transliteration: Valaid langhiya farangeen hatth onaan, mulk qaum layi raah najaat di labbh
Yaad phullaan de naal saja dharti, raahon kande hata ke sab de sab
translation: Go abroad, cross to the foreigners' lands, and find a way to save your country and people.
Decorate your homeland with flowers of remembrance, and clear every thorn from its paths.
couplets.story: When you go to foreign countries, use what you learn to help your own country. Remember home, and make it more beautiful by clearing problems out of its way, like thorns off a road.

original: ویری تیرے تے گھات اے لائی بیٹھا منوں بغض کدورتے وی دے تب
احمدؔ دا ایہی غلام جیکر کرم آپ کرے تیرے حال تے رب
transliteration: Vairi tere te ghaat ae laai baitha, manon bughz kadoorat vi de tab
Ahmad da ehi ghulaam, jekar karam aap kare tere haal te Rab
translation: Your enemy is lying in wait for you; give up spite and resentment in your heart.
Ahmad's only wish: may God Himself show kindness to you in your situation.
couplets.story: There will be people who wish you harm. Don't fill your heart with hate in return. The poet's one wish is that God Himself will look after the person who is leaving.

deeper: The poem ends with a prayer: may God take care of the traveller. Giving up hatred even toward enemies is a real Islamic and Sufi teaching. Remembering your homeland and serving it from far away is presented as a duty of the heart.
why: Many families today have someone living abroad. This poem says what a lot of parents and grandparents feel but don't always put into words.
prompt: If you moved far away, what would you want to carry with you from home?
notes: The last two couplets are hard to read in places; their general sense is clear.
